# enco:plugin@0.6.0

Enco plugin contract. Plugins interact with the host only through these imports.

## Worlds

### `base`

Imports and lifecycle operations shared by all plugins.

- Imports: types, host
- Exports: lifecycle

### `provider-plugin`

A plugin exposing completion and embedding operations.

- Imports: types, host

#### enum `effect`

Mutation semantics used to order calls and settle interrupted work.

Consecutive read-only calls run together; other calls run one at a time. A call cut off by
a crash fails as retryable when it is read-only, and settles as unknown otherwise.

- `read-only`: Changes nothing beyond its result.
- `idempotent`: Making the call again has the same effect as making it once.
- `side-effect`: Changes something that must not be changed again blindly.

#### record `tool-spec`

A tool disclosed to the model.

`input-schema` describes the argument object in a subset of JSON Schema:
- objects with `properties` and `required`, always with `additionalProperties: false`;
- strings with `enum`, `minLength` and `maxLength`;
- integers and numbers with `minimum` and `maximum`;
- booleans;
- arrays with `items`, `minItems` and `maxItems`;
- `anyOf` with two or more schemas.

Any schema below the root may carry a `description` and a `default` that fits it; the root
is an object and carries neither. A declaration outside the subset fails to load. The host
checks every call against the schema before the plugin sees it: an optional property given
as null counts as not given, and an integer written with a zero fraction, such as 5.0,
arrives as 5.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The name the model calls the tool by: ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, unique among the plugin's tools. |
| `description` | `string` | What the tool does, for the model to read. |
| `input-schema` | `json` | The argument object, in the subset of JSON Schema stated above. |
| `effect` | `effect` | What a call may change; completion adapters ignore it, and the host uses it when dispatching. |

#### variant `outcome`

A known result, a known failure, or an external effect that cannot be confirmed.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | `json` | The call succeeded with this JSON result. |
| `failed` | `failure` | The call failed, and its effects are known. |
| `unknown` | `failure` | An external effect may have happened and cannot be confirmed; it is never retried automatically. |

|---|---|---|

| `model` | `string` | The model the service runs. |
| `options` | `json` | Options the adapter merges into its request, as a JSON object. |

#### func `config`

```wit
config: func() -> json;
```

The configuration of this invocation's generation, excluding credential mappings.

#### func `log`

```wit
log: func(level: log-level, message: string);
```

Write a diagnostic to the host log.

#### func `http`

```wit
http: async func(request: http-request) -> result<http-response, http-failure>;
```

Send a request and collect its response; non-2xx statuses are returned as responses.

The host attaches declared credentials only to the bound origin (scheme, host and port),
overriding the matching request header. Redirects are followed only within that origin.
Cross-origin redirects are returned unchanged. Credential values in response headers,
bodies and failures are replaced with [redacted:<environment variable name>].
Encoded forms of a credential (such as base64) are not redacted.

### `tools`

Model-facing tools whose definitions are fixed with their generation.

#### func `list`

```wit
list: func(config: json) -> list<tool-spec>;
```

Project tool definitions from configuration already accepted by `lifecycle.describe`.

Definitions are fixed with the generation, so this runs without network access.

#### func `call`

```wit
call: async func(name: string, input: json) -> outcome;
```

Execute one tool.

`input` already fits the tool's `input-schema`; validate only what the schema cannot
express. Return an unknown outcome when an external effect may have occurred but is
unconfirmed.

# Errors
Failure codes are `provider.network`, `provider.auth`, `provider.rate_limited`,
`provider.server`, `provider.bad_request`, `provider.bad_response`, and `timeout`.

### `embedding`

Embeds texts for retrieval independently of model completion.

#### func `embed`

```wit
embed: async func(settings: settings, inputs: list<string>) -> result<list<list<f32>>, failure>;
```

Return exactly one nonempty vector of finite numbers per input, in input order.
All returned vectors must have the same width.

# Errors
Uses `provider.*` failure codes and `timeout`, as in `completion.complete`.

#### record `question`

Instructions and the allowed answer shape for one independent judgment.

#### variant `answer`

An answer to one question, as probabilities, or a refusal.

Probabilities are finite and in [0, 1]; choice and score distributions sum to one

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `predicate` | `f64` | The probability of yes. |
| `choice` | `list<f64>` | One probability per option, in label order. |
| `score` | `list<f64>` | One probability per level, in label order. |
| `refused` | `_` | The service declined to answer this question. |

#### func `decide`

```wit
decide: async func(settings: settings, state: string, questions: list<question>) -> result<list<answer>, failure>;
```

Evaluate each question against the same text state. Return one matching answer
per question in input order; any question may instead receive `refused`.

# Errors
Uses `provider.*` failure codes and `timeout`, as in `completion.complete`.

### `lifecycle`

Describes and checks the component without assigning its registry identity.

#### record `credential`

Named credential attached to `origin`, or to the caller-selected service when absent.

A fixed origin uses the generation's secret mapping; an absent origin uses the endpoint's.
Names and origins must be unique, including at most one absent origin.
The host sets `header` to `prefix` followed by the credential value; plugins never see it.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The name the owner's configuration maps to an environment variable. |
| `origin` | `option<string>` | The origin the credential is sent to; absent for the service the caller selects. |
| `header` | `string` | The request header that carries the credential. |
| `prefix` | `string` | Text placed before the credential value in the header, such as `Bearer `. |
| `required` | `bool` | Whether the plugin cannot work without it. |

#### record `description`

Plugin-wide facts and requirements.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `summary` | `string` | One line on what the plugin offers. |
| `config-schema` | `json` | The configuration the plugin accepts, as JSON Schema; only `describe` validates it. |
| `credentials` | `list<credential>` | The credentials the plugin uses. |

#### func `describe`

```wit
describe: func(config: json) -> result<description, failure>;
```

Describe the component or reject its configuration.

An empty object must be accepted and provide the plugin's minimum capabilities.
Declarations are fixed with the generation, so this runs without network access.

#### func `probe`

```wit
probe: async func() -> result<_, failure>;
```

Check the component without network access or owner-specific configuration.

### `composer`

Writes the model requests of the Sessions whose profile names this plugin.

A composition is a pure function of its arguments, the plugin's configuration and its own code,
and changes nothing but its result: it has no files, no environment variables and no network, so
`host.http` fails. The wall clock reads the Round's instant, the monotonic clock stands still and
randomness is seeded by the Round, so the same generation, called again within a Round with the
same arguments, returns the same plan.

The host records each plan before sending it and resolves its Log references. A plan breaks
this contract when it discloses a capability outside this Round, refers to a position outside
the transcript, or sends images to a model that does not accept them; when a reply plan leaves
out a capability in `lifeline`; or when a compaction discloses any tool or stops where no Round
ends.

#### record `compose-input`

Everything the host supplies for one composition.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `session` | `session` | The Session the request is for. |
| `timezone` | `string` | The owner's time zone, as an IANA name such as `Asia/Shanghai`. |
| `home` | `string` | The home's absolute path on the node running this Round.  Its layout is part of this contract: `config.toml`, `AGENTS.md` for the standing instructions, `plugins/<name>/`, `sdk/`, `manual/` and `workspace/`. `.data/` is Enco's own store and not part of it. |
| `transcript` | `transcript` | The history a plan may refer to. |
| `previous` | `option<plan>` | This Session's latest recorded reply plan; absent at the start, or when it could not be read, which `omitted` then says. |
| `instructions` | `option<string>` | The text of `AGENTS.md`, as read at the start of this Round; absent when the file does not exist, and in safe mode. |
| `memories` | `list<memory>` | Memories for this Round in priority order: pinned ones first, then those recalled for the latest input, most relevant first; empty in safe mode. |
| `omitted` | `list<omission>` | Content the host could not supply; the host records it with the plan. |
| `capabilities` | `list<capability>` | Every tool this Round may disclose; in safe mode, only the lifeline. |
| `lifeline` | `list<capability-id>` | The tools every reply plan must disclose; empty when the Session does not require the lifeline. |
| `unavailable` | `list<unavailable-plugin>` | Plugins left out of this Round. |
| `safe-mode` | `option<safe-mode>` | Why this Round runs in safe mode; absent in normal operation. |
| `reply` | `reply-target` | The model a reply plan is for. |
| `compaction` | `option<budget>` | The summarizing model's limits; absent when no summarizing model is usable. |
| `compactions-left` | `u32` | How many more compactions this Round allows. |

#### record `compaction`

A request to summarize history before replying.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `upto` | `log-pos` | The last Round end to summarize, one of `transcript.round-ends`. |
| `plan` | `plan` | The summarizing request; it discloses no tools. |

#### variant `composition`

What a composition returns.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `reply` | `plan` | A reply request. |
| `compact` | `compaction` | Summarize history first; the host composes again once the summary is recorded. |

#### func `options-schema`

```wit
options-schema: func(config: json) -> json;
```

The JSON Schema of the options a profile passes to `compose`, in the subset `tool-spec`
states.

An empty object must fit it. The host checks a profile's options against the schema of the
generation that runs them: registering configuration or code that breaks a profile's options
is rejected, and a profile whose options no longer fit, as after a rollback, cannot use this
plugin until they do. The schema is fixed with the generation, so this runs without network
access.

#### func `compose`

```wit
compose: func(options: json, input: compose-input) -> result<composition, failure>;
```

Write the next request.

`options` fit the running generation's `options-schema` and are normalized as tool arguments
are. Return `compact` only while `compaction` is present and `compactions-left` is above
zero.

# Errors
`context.overflow` when no valid request fits the window; when only a compaction would make
it fit and `compaction` is absent, the host records why no summarizing model is usable. The
host records any other code as `compose.failed`.
